exercises.name: Jump Rope

source_english.description: Turn the rope with the hands and make light repeated jumps as it passes beneath the feet.
instructions: Hold the handles of the jump rope with your hands, palms facing inward.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Swing the rope over your head and jump over it as it comes towards your feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and repeat the jump as the rope comes around again.
Continue jumping for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep a steady rhythm.
Land or pedal softly.
Breathe continuously.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a pace and surface that allow controlled breathing and stable landings.

exercises.name: Jump Shrug

source_english.description: A barbell jump shrug combines explosive hip and knee extension with a powerful shoulder shrug before a soft landing.
instructions: Stand with the barbell at the thighs, feet about hip-width apart, and hands just outside the legs.
Dip slightly at the knees and hips while keeping the back neutral.
Drive through the floor, extend the hips and knees, and shrug the shoulders as the bar rises.
Land softly with bent knees and lower the bar under control.
form_cues: Keep the bar close.
Finish tall through the hips before the shrug.
Land quietly with the knees aligned.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms before extending the hips.
Jumping forward or letting the bar drift away.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load and clear the landing area before performing the jump.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean

source_english.description: A kettlebell clean uses a hip-driven close path to bring the bell from between the legs into the rack position.
instructions: Stand with the kettlebell between your feet and hinge at the hips with a neutral back.
Hike the bell back, then drive the hips forward to guide it upward close to the body.
Rotate the hand around the handle and receive the bell softly against the forearm in the rack position.
Lower it back between the legs with control and repeat on the same or opposite side.
form_cues: Use the hips rather than an arm curl.
Keep the bell close to the body.
Relax the grip as the bell rotates.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell swing far forward.
Catching it with a bent wrist.
Squatting under the bell instead of hinging.
source_english.safety_note: Start with a light kettlebell and keep the forearm and wrist aligned in the rack.

source_english.description: Hinge the hips to load the kettlebell behind you, then drive forward so it floats to shoulder height.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping your arms straight and maintaining a flat back.
Drive your hips forward and swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height, using the momentum generated by your hips.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back down between your legs and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the trunk braced.
Let the hips drive the kettlebell; do not lift it with the arms.
Finish each repetition under control.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: A Turkish get-up moves from the floor to standing and back while one kettlebell remains locked overhead.
instructions: Lie on your back with the kettlebell locked out over one shoulder and the same-side knee bent.
Press through the foot to lift the hips, then sweep the opposite leg under into a supported half-kneel.
Rotate upright, stand while keeping the kettlebell overhead, and stabilize.
Reverse the sequence step by step to return to the floor, then switch sides.
form_cues: Keep the trunk braced.
Keep the kettlebell vertically above the shoulder through each floor-to-stand transition.
Finish each repetition under control.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.
